title: Leaky user functions and LEAKPROOF marking (correctness, not speed)
issue: A user-supplied non-leakproof function must never be evaluated on rows the policy hides. Marking such a function LEAKPROOF (perf hack) lets it run before the policy;
symptom: Each query returns (visible rows, leaked) where leaked = number of times the spy function saw a hidden row. The correct answer is leaked = 0. Variants where the hash differs from no_rls_baseline leak (or raise an error that carries a hidden value).

scale.meaning: number of rows in app.docs (10 orgs; user N is a member of org N only)
